title: Negative $β$-transformations: invariant measures, matching properties and associated subshifts
summary: For a real number $β>1$, we study the negative $β$-transformations, defined by $T_{-β}(x) := -βx + \lfloorβx\rfloor + 1$ for $x \in (0,1]$. It is known that for each $β>1$, there exists a unique $T_{-β}$-invariant probability measure which is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure, denoted by $ν_{-β}$. For two distinct non-integer real numbers $β_2>β_1>1$, we prove that $ν_{-β_1}=ν_{-β_2}$ if and only if $β_1$ is a root of the quadratic equation $x^2 - qx - p = 0$ (where $p, q \in \mathbb{N}$ and $p \leq q$) and $β_2 = β_1 + 1$.
